meta.title: x/tools/gopls/internal/analysis/modernize: fmtappendf suggests invalid fix
meta.fix_ref: golang/tools@e48606bae176 (gopls/internal/analysis/modernize: invalid code produced by fmtappendf modernizer; CL 697342)
meta.build_notes: go install golang.org/x/tools/gopls@<version> with the local Go (go1.27.1), which builds both; the server runs the local go command. Reported 2025-07-22 against the analyzer at x/tools master; v0.20.0 was tagged 2025-07-28 with the fmtappendf pass (modernize.go calls fmtappendf(pass)); the fix merged 2025-08-20, v0.21.0 was tagged 2025-12-05.
meta.notes: The fix deletes "[]byte(" and ")" around the fmt.Sprintf call; a conversion may carry a trailing comma inside its parentheses (T(x,)), which the pre-fix edit left behind on its own line. The fixed analyzer also deletes the text between the argument and the right parenthesis.

settings_note: The modernize analyzer is on by default in both builds.

files.source: issue body, first code block (output of 'cat b.go', the shell prompt line omitted)

files.note: a module around the file (the reporter ran in the x/tools module); go 1.24 (fmtappendf needs go1.19)

repro.steps: Open b.go. The fmtappendf pass reports the multi-line conversion []byte(\n fmt.Sprintf("%d", 0),\n) ('Replace []byte(fmt.Sprintf...) with fmt.Appendf'). Apply its fix. Reported (with the modernize command): the conversion's trailing comma is left on its own line ('Bytes:' / 'fmt.Appendf(nil, "%d", 0),' / ','), which does not parse. Probe: the edited text must have no parse error that the original did not have.
